slow.title: Slow values from the display
slow.description:
Modbus is read continuously and handles all control. The display's web interface additionally carries values Modbus does not have, such as delivered heat.

The catch is that only the page the panel is showing stays fresh, so the integration has to walk there and back. The panel moves while it does. Tick the pages you want, or skip this step and run on Modbus alone.

The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data, where delivered heat is counted.

{count} pages were found on the {model}.

confirm.title: Add {model}?
confirm.description: A CTC display was found at {host}. Setting it up walks the unit's menu to see what it can report, so the panel will move for a moment.

error.not_a_ctc: That address answers, but it is not a CTC display.
error.modbus_failed: The display answers but Modbus does not. Turn it on from the panel under Installer, Define, Remote control, where Ethernet must be set to Modbus TCP.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up.
abort.not_a_ctc: The device is not a CTC display.

data_description.enable_control: Creates control entities that write to CTC's volatile 1000 registers. The controller forgets them about five minutes after the last write, so control releases itself if Home Assistant stops. The stored settings in the 61500 block are never written.
data_description.send_statistics: One report per day to {endpoint}: the integration's version, the Home Assistant version, installation type and Python version, the language and the country you configured in Home Assistant, an approximate position rounded to about 11 km, the number of entities and devices, which transports are in use, whether control is enabled, how many display pages are harvested, whether the row with the unit's operating hours was recognised on the history page, whether the counters behind the coefficient of performance were found on the display or in Modbus and whether each handed over a number at the last read, and when there is no figure, why: too little energy counted so far, a counter standing still although the unit has been running, or a quotient no heat pump could produce. Also the number of failed register reads, the indoor and outdoor unit's model, the firmware in the display, the heat pump's control board and the control unit, the product and the year and week of manufacture from the serial number, and the coefficient of performance (COP) over the last day, a rolling year, the machine's first year and the lifetime. One measurement leaves the house, and only when it is wrong: where a counter stands still or the two counters give an impossible quotient, the two lifetime totals in kilowatt hours are sent along with the flag, never otherwise. Never a name, an address, an exact position, a full serial number, an entity name or a page name, never anything finer than one day, and your IP address is not stored. It also sends a random id created when the integration was installed, so that the daily reports can be kept apart and erased on request (the server keeps it only as a hash, and it says nothing about who you are), a hash that links the beolink plugins running on the same Home Assistant, how many warnings and errors the integration logged since the previous report, and whether it is running or waiting to start again, never the messages themselves or the reason. Switching this off also erases what has already been sent. The full list: {privacy_url}
data_description.visit_system_info: The panel walks to the display's System information page once and back, to read the serial number and the display's own software version. It presses nothing but Advanced, Display and System information, checks where the panel went after every press, and gives up at the first surprise.
data_description.check_updates: Asks GitHub once a day whether a newer release of this integration exists, and says so in the repairs view. Home Assistant only offers updates for what HACS installed, so a copy put in place by hand is otherwise never offered one.

rescan.title: Slow values from the display
rescan.description: {count} pages were found. The panel was moved during the scan and put back. The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data.

abort.panel_busy: The panel is in use right now: the integration is reading the display's pages or walking its menu. Try again in a moment. Nothing has been changed.

pages_missing.title: No page of the display is being read
pages_missing.description: Not one of the display's pages is ticked, so the display is never read: delivered heat, and with it the coefficient of performance, lives only there. Tick the pages under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure. Is the list empty, the menu could not be read when the integration was set up; reload the integration and it reads the menu again.

history_page_missing.title: The coefficient of performance is missing its history page
history_page_missing.description: The coefficient of performance is worked out from the display's counter for delivered heat, which lives on the page with the stored or historical operation data. That page is not being read. Tick it under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure.

identity_incomplete.title: The serial number has not been read
identity_incomplete.description: The display writes the serial number and its own software version into the System information page only once that page has been shown on the panel. Open it once on the panel, or let the integration walk there itself under Configure.

update_available.title: A newer version of CTC Local Easyconf is out
update_available.description: Version {latest} has been released; this is {installed}. Installed through HACS: update it there, under Settings, Devices and services, HACS. Installed by hand: replace custom_components/ctc_ecozenith with the new release and restart Home Assistant.
